title: Cold install test, fixes, and version 1.0.0
description: The final check. A fresh session with no project context and only the published documentation and release installs the product on a clean virtual machine: installs, completes setup for a BHPLTA club, invites a captain, generates a player link, makes and restores a backup, switches tournaments on, and performs an upgrade from the previous pre-release. Every point where it hesitates, guesses or fails is logged. A second session with full context fixes the docs or the product for each one, and the test is repeated until it passes without intervention. Then cut 1.0.0. Using a less capable model with no context is deliberate: it stands in for a newcomer and will not paper over gaps with background knowledge.

recommended_model.name: Sonnet 5.5
recommended_model.rationale: The tester should resemble a newcomer; fixes found may be routed to a stronger model as needed.

acceptance_criteria: A clean-machine install following only the published docs completes every listed task without help
Every stumble from each run is recorded with the fix made (doc or product)
The final run needed no intervention
Jim has reviewed the final run log and agreed to release
v1.0.0 is tagged and published with complete upgrade notes
sprints/INDEX.md and the sprint files are marked completed

notes: Give the testing session only the README link and the release page - not this repository's working tree, CLAUDE.md or sprint files.
Use a throwaway VM or container with a self-signed or local certificate arrangement described in the install guide's 'trying it locally' section.

testing_requirements: The cold install itself, repeated until clean

context.user_story: As a new club, I want proof that the instructions work for someone who has never seen the project.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
